**Instructions.** Complete this assignment in Quarto or R Markdown and submit
a rendered PDF to Gradescope. Show your code. Interpretation questions are
graded on precision (adjusted for what, units, association vs causation,
population), exactly as practiced in Labs 2 and 3. End with your AI-use
statement (see Section 4).

**Data.** The Baystate Medical Center birth weight study (Springfield, MA,
1986), 189 births:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data(birthwt, package = "MASS")
births <- birthwt |>
  mutate(smoke = factor(smoke, labels = c("Non-smoker", "Smoker")))
```

Variables used below: `bwt` = birth weight (grams), `lwt` = mother's
pre-pregnancy weight (pounds), `age` = mother's age (years), `smoke` =
smoking during pregnancy.

# Section 1: Do (6 points)

**1.1** Describe the outcome `bwt`: a histogram plus a short numerical summary.
Two sentences on center, spread, and shape, with units. (2 pts)

**1.2** Fit the simple linear regression of `bwt` on `lwt`. Report the fitted
equation and add the fitted line to a scatterplot (use your coefficients with
`geom_abline`, not `geom_smooth`). (2 pts)

**1.3** Using arithmetic on your coefficients, give the model's expected birth
weight for mothers weighing 120 and 200 pounds. State which prediction you
trust more, and why, referring to the data. (2 pts)

# Section 2: Interpret (8 points; interpretation precision counts double)

**2.1** Interpret the slope from 1.2 in one strong-form sentence. (2 pts)

**2.2** The R-squared of this model is about 0.03. A journalist concludes the
model is "useless." Give a two-sentence rebuttal that concedes what the model
cannot do and states what the slope estimate still offers. (2 pts)

**2.3** Fit `bwt ~ smoke`, then `bwt ~ smoke + lwt`. Report the smoking
coefficient from both. Does adjusting for mother's weight change the smoking
association much here? Using the group means of `lwt` by smoking status,
explain in one sentence why the adjustment behaves the way it does. (2 pts)

**2.4** Write the strong-form interpretation of the smoking coefficient in the
adjusted model, then a second sentence stating clearly one reason this is not
an estimate of the causal effect of smoking cessation. (2 pts)

# Section 3: Critique the AI (6 points)

A student pasted this dataset description into an AI assistant and asked for
an analysis. The assistant replied:

> "I fit a regression of birth weight on mother's age and found a slope of
> 12.4 grams per year. Since the intercept is 2656 grams, a newborn whose
> mother is age zero would weigh 2656 grams. The p-value for age was 0.19,
> which proves that mother's age has no effect on birth weight. Because
> heavier mothers tend to be older, I also recommend removing `lwt` from any
> model that includes `age`, since two correlated predictors cannot be used
> together in linear regression. Overall, since this regression is based on a
> proper hospital sample, the slope of 12.4 tells us how much a mother's
> baby will gain if she delays pregnancy by one year."

**3.1** This paragraph contains at least four distinct statistical errors.
Identify each one you find (quote the offending phrase), and explain in one or
two sentences why it is wrong. Finding four earns full credit; a fifth earns a
bonus point. (4 pts + 1 bonus)

**3.2** Verify one of the AI's numerical claims by fitting `bwt ~ age`
yourself. Report whether the slope and intercept match, and write the correct
one-sentence conclusion about the age association that the data actually
support. (2 pts)

# Section 4: AI-use statement (required, ungraded)

One or two sentences: which AI tools you used on this assignment and for what,
or "No AI tools used." Note that Section 3 asks you to critique provided AI
output; using an AI to critique the AI is permitted, but the errors you report
are yours to defend.
